entries.note: Neither “simple statistical matching” nor what would demonstrate understanding is defined sufficiently for a shared test of this necessity claim.

entries.test: Comparative outputs from original Imagen and Imagen 4 would establish text-rendering improvements, and Marcus’s four published horse-riding-astronaut outputs would establish the reported failures.
entries.note: The four failures concern his reported attempts, not every possible generation.

entries.test: Published outputs on the cited noncanonical prompts would show whether Imagen 4 correctly depicts their requested relationships and improves substantially over earlier outputs.
entries.note: The proposition drops “some” and supplies a comparison with earlier models where the immediate comparison is ambiguous.

entries.test: Comparative text-rendering results and Imagen 4 outputs for watch prompts specifying times other than 10:10 would establish the claimed improvement and persistent time-depiction failures.
entries.note: The proposition extends an Imagen 4 discussion to image generators generally. “Dreadful” has a testable performance reading here: repeatedly showing the wrong requested time.

entries.test: The published Imagen 4 block image can be compared with the prompt’s specified colors, shapes, and spatial relationships.
entries.note: Read in context, this describes a demonstrated failure on the cited prompt.

entries.test: Imagen 4’s documented capabilities and public evaluations would establish whether it is a specialized image generator or exhibits general intelligence across domains.
entries.note: The punchy wording still asserts that Imagen 4 is not AGI; its narrow capabilities provide a plain test in this case.

entries.test: Published o3 outputs on the original examples and the new woman-and-watch prompt would show comparative successes and whether the new image satisfies all requested details.
entries.note: The attribution to o3 records Marcus’s claim, irrespective of which underlying system generated the images.

entries.test: The published ChatGPT exchange and images would show whether it acknowledged the error and continued depicting a tree growing out of the monkey.
entries.note: Acknowledgment is observable in the dialogue and does not require establishing a private mental state.

entries.test: Public evaluations that isolate interpretation of prompt relationships from image rendering would test whether persistent interpretation errors cause failures to follow arbitrary prompts.
entries.note: Output errors alone establish unreliability more readily than they establish its claimed cause.

entries.test: The published Sora and Veo clips would show whether the requested phrase is visibly handwritten into the planner’s 9am slot, including whether Veo displays it from the start.
entries.note: “Either” endorses the preceding implication that Sora also failed the task.

entries.test: Google’s 2022 announcement and public evaluations of image generators available by June 2025 would show what was promised and whether systems reliably rendered the semantic details of varied prompts.
entries.note: The surrounding examples give reliability a concrete reading: consistently satisfying requested objects, attributes, text, and relationships.
